proposals.title: Resolve TASK-0001's two persistent review blockers: package-manager executable and tsconfig source-extension coverage
proposals.why_now: Two consecutive implementation attempts (attempt-01 and attempt-02) and two reviews have been blocked by the same two findings: (1) the authoritative review environment cannot execute pnpm commands because '/workspace/pnpm' is not a valid Node.js module, and (2) every workspace tsconfig's include pattern covers only '*.ts', so .tsx, .mts, and .cts files are silently excluded from compilation — a violation of the must-preserve requirement that newly added source cannot bypass gates. Thirteen cycles have elapsed with zero committed code. This is the only path to unblocking all other FASE-1 work. The fix for finding (1) is to replace pnpm workspaces with npm workspaces, which is built into every Node.js installation and requires no separate executable. The fix for finding (2) is to expand every tsconfig include to '**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}' and add a configuration test proving coverage. No new production logic is introduced.

proposals.title: Write the three DEFINIR ADRs required before packages/core can be implemented
proposals.why_now: ADR-002 requires the rand() hash function to be specified bit-exactly in an ADR before any implementation of rand() is written — any choice embedded in code without an ADR cannot be changed without an encodingVersion bump that invalidates all future reference StateHashes. ADR-009 is an explicit FASE-1 acceptance criterion: the CanonicalEncoder must be specified in its own ADR before any state hash exists. ADR-004 requires the mechanism for making division-without-rounding-mode a type or lint error to be decided before arithmetic helpers are written, because the division API shape depends on this choice. All three must precede packages/core work. These ADRs are pure documentation, depend only on the workspace existing, and can be proposed and written in the same cycle that resolves IDEA-001.

proposals.title: packages/core — branded numeric types, positional RNG, CanonicalEncoder, and arithmetic helpers
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the sole dependency of packages/world, packages/domain, packages/narrative, and packages/contracts. Without branded bigint types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate) and branded safe-integer types (Tick and noise/index types), the type system cannot enforce ADR-003 or ADR-004 and downstream packages will silently mix incompatible numeric representations. Without the positional rand() matching ADR-002 bit-exactly, packages/world cannot be written. Without CanonicalEncoder per ADR-009, no StateHash can be produced and INV-01, INV-17, and INV-22 have no foundation. This is the single highest-leverage implementation deliverable in FASE-1 and must precede all domain and world work.

proposals.title: packages/world, packages/domain, packages/application — price generator, double-entry ledger, canonical tick loop, and save format
proposals.why_now: These three packages compose the functional FASE-1 simulation core and must be delivered together because packages/application is the only layer that can compose packages/world and packages/domain without coupling them (Section 14.5 prohibits world from knowing domain and vice versa). The price generator is the entry point for INV-02 — explicitly described by the spec as the most important test in the project. The double-entry ledger is the entry point for INV-04 through INV-07. The canonical tick loop from Section 7 implements the ten-step locked order, which is a named FASE-1 acceptance criterion. The save format per ADR-006 with INV-21 enforcement is required before tools/replay can exist.

proposals.title: tools/replay, tools/bench with frozen calibration ratios, and minimum Electron UI to complete FASE-1 acceptance
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires: (1) tools/replay that compares two executions and reports the first divergent tick, (2) tools/bench with calibration micro-benchmark and performance ratios frozen in a versioned file, and (3) a minimum UI with price chart via lightweight-charts, player BRL balance, buy/sell market order buttons, pause and 1x time controls, and the permanent non-dismissable disclaimer required by Section 20. The spec warns (Section 14.6) that deferring the Windows/Linux installer past FASE-1 leads to unrecoverable ABI and packaging failures. The performance baseline frozen in tools/bench has no reference to compare against for the rest of the project if deferred. INV-19 (same StateHash on Windows and Linux, simulation-worker vs CLI replay) requires the cross-platform CI matrix that depends on both tools/replay and the Electron shell existing.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — transcendental functions: Section 5.1 constructs prices in log-space (requiring log and exp), but Section 13 prohibits Math.log, Math.exp, and Math.pow in all pure packages. An ADR specifying a fixed-point or linear-interpolation-over-lookup-table implementation that produces bit-identical results across platforms must be written before packages/world work begins. This ADR is not listed in the spec's known-gaps section but is a necessary consequence of Sections 5.1 and 13 read together. Implementing packages/world before this ADR exists will violate either Section 13 or INV-19.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — octave parameters: the number of octaves, their block periods, and their amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR per Section 5.1. These must be recorded in a versioned configuration file with an ADR before the price generator is implemented, because any parameter change after tools/bench freezes the performance baseline requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — hash function: ADR-002 requires the hash function to be specified bit-exactly in an ADR before any rand() implementation. As of CYCLE-000013 no such ADR exists. Any rand() written without it embeds an unrecorded decision that cannot be changed without a breaking encodingVersion bump invalidating future saved games and CI reference hashes.
